task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-03 Step 1b) on ISS-0442's design (lib/letflow/design/iss0442-lint-handoffs-minimal-diff-autofix.md): verify the depth-aware raw-text substitution algorithm is sound against the demonstrated PASS/PASS nested-collision risk, verify the Jason.OrderedObject/mix.lock claim, verify all 4 acceptance criteria are covered, confirm no literal implementation code, and judge whether the new function shapes are unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV.
acceptance_criteria: Depth-aware substitution algorithm hand-traced against a constructed top-level-status + nested result.status example, including escaped quotes and string values containing braces/colons, and confirmed sound

result.summary: One BLOCKER found; algorithm itself is sound. DEPTH-TRACKING ALGORITHM (Section 2.2): hand-traced against a constructed example `{"status": "PASS", "result": {"status": "PASS", "note": "contains a brace { and a quote \" and colon: literally"}}`. Walk: root `{` -> depth=1. Depth-1 string "status" followed by ':' -> KEY, content matches "status" -> candidate #1 (top-level). Its value "PASS" is a depth-1 VALUE (not followed by ':'), correctly associated with candidate #1. Depth-1 string "result" followed by ':' -> KEY, not "status", ignored; then '{' -> depth=2. Inside depth 2: string "status" followed by ':' is a KEY, but at depth 2, not depth 1, so per the design's explicit depth==1 gate it is correctly EXCLUDED from candidacy -- this is exactly the PASS/PASS collision ISSUE-FIXER demonstrated, and the design closes it structurally, not by luck of file order. The "note" value string containing `{`, `"` (escaped) and a literal `:` is consumed entirely by the string-scanning sub-state (consume until next UNESCAPED quote, treating `\` as a 2-char-escape starter) before the depth-counting logic ever sees its interior characters -- so the embedded `{` does not perturb `depth`, and the embedded `:` does not falsely mark anything a KEY, because it is never examined as 'the character following a string's closing quote' (the string hasn't closed yet at that point). This is correct. Escape handling generalizes correctly even though the design's 'two-character escape' framing under-describes `\uXXXX` (a 6-char escape, not 2): traced this explicitly -- consuming only `\u` as the 2-char unit and then scanning the following 4 hex digits as ordinary characters is harmless, because hex digits (0-9a-fA-F) can never themselves be a quote or a backslash, so no false string-boundary or false-escape can result. Whitespace/newline-between-key-and-colon handling (skip whitespace after closing quote, then require ':') is explicit and correct. Last-key-wins duplicate handling mirrors Jason.decode/1's own semantics as claimed. CONCLUSION: the algorithm is genuinely sound against every edge case in the task brief (escaped quotes, string-embedded braces/colons, whitespace variation); this is not a rubber stamp -- I hand-traced it token by token. JASON.ORDEREDOBJECT CLAIM -- BLOCKER: the design doc (section 1.1, 'Version check (per ISSUE-FIXER, re-confirmed here)') states 'mix.lock currently pins jason 1.4.5, which does not include Jason.OrderedObject (that landed later in the 1.x line)'. This is FACTUALLY WRONG and directly checkable in this repo: deps/jason/lib/ordered_object.ex exists, fully implements Jason.OrderedObject (Access behaviour, Enumerable-like keyword wrapper); deps/jason/CHANGELOG.md shows OrderedObject shipped in **1.3.0** (21.12.2021) -- three minor versions before 1.4.5 (05.05.2026, per this same CHANGELOG), not 'later in the 1.x line'. deps/jason/lib/jason.ex:19,51 documents the `objects: :ordered_objects` decode option and deps/jason/lib/encode.ex:250 implements the Encoder clause for the struct -- it is fully present and usable at the exact pinned version (1.4.5), not merely declared. This repeats, one level down, exactly the failure class ISS-0442's own design doc was created to close in reviewability terms and that WF02-REQ168's validator gate previously blocked on (a live-verification claim presented as confirmed fact that a direct, cheap check in this same repo disproves). It also means the design's own acceptance criterion ('jason dependency version/capability for option (a) checked against what mix.exs/mix.lock actually pin') is not actually satisfied -- the check was performed but produced and asserted a wrong conclusion. NOTE: this does NOT change the final recommendation of option (b) -- the design's OTHER, independent reason for rejecting (a) (effect (2) pretty-print reflow is untouched by ordered-key preservation, since Jason.encode!(..., pretty: true) does compact-encode-then-reformat via Jason.Formatter.pretty_print_to_iodata regardless of key order -- confirmed by reading deps/jason/lib/jason.ex:217-226 and deps/jason/lib/formatter.ex myself) is correct and independently sufficient to reject (a). But a design document cannot assert a specific, checkable technical fact incorrectly and still pass this gate, even when the wrong fact does not change the final choice -- a reader (ELIXIR-DEV, a future auditor) has no way to distinguish this false claim from the surrounding true ones without re-deriving it, which is exactly what this gate exists to do once. OTHER CHECKS, ALL PASS: (3) 4 acceptance criteria re-derived from ISS-0442.yaml's own text (real recommendation with tradeoffs -- yes, section 1; jason version checked against mix.exs/mix.lock -- performed but wrong, see BLOCKER; substitution position-precise and specified precisely enough for ELIXIR-DEV -- yes, verified by hand-trace above; FAIL/missing/null/non-string refusal preserved -- yes, section 3 confirmed against the real autofix_file/1 case expression at lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:414-446, only the is_map_key(@autofix_map, status) branch's action changes; no-flag CI path preserved -- yes, confirmed run/1's `if autofix?` guard (read the real file) means run_autofix/1 and everything downstream of it including the new functions are never invoked without --autofix; no implementation code -- confirmed, grepped the whole .md for defmodule/def/end and literal Elixir bodies, found only function-name/arity references and @spec-shaped prose, consistent with this project's design-doc convention). (4) verified: no .ex implementation code in the design doc. (5) Open questions (exact exception type; suggested regression fixtures) are genuinely minor and do not need resolution before implementation: the exception-type choice does not change behavior observable by any caller (the design already mandates 'raise loudly, never fall back to whole-file re-encode', which is the load-bearing invariant; whether it's raise/1 or Mix.raise/1 is pure style), and regression fixtures are explicitly TEST-DESIGNER's job in a later WF-03 step, not something this design needs to specify. Also confirmed algorithm plugs into the REAL current code: read lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex directly -- write_json!/2 (line 454-457) and its sole call site (line 420) match the design's description exactly, and `raw` is indeed already bound in autofix_file/1's own with-clause (line 415) as the design claims, so no extra file read is introduced.

issues.description: Design doc section 1.1 states 'Jason.OrderedObject is not present in 1.4.5 (shipped later in the 1.x line)'. This is false: deps/jason/CHANGELOG.md shows OrderedObject shipped in Jason 1.3.0 (21.12.2021), and deps/jason/lib/ordered_object.ex plus the objects: :ordered_objects decode option (deps/jason/lib/jason.ex:19,51) and the Encoder clause for it (deps/jason/lib/encode.ex:250) are all present and fully usable in the exact vendored/pinned 1.4.5. Fix: rewrite section 1.1's version-check paragraph to state correctly that Jason.OrderedObject IS available at the currently pinned 1.4.5 (no mix.lock bump needed for that reason), and re-ground the rejection of option (a) entirely on the effect-(2) pretty-print-reflow argument (which is correct and independently sufficient -- Jason.encode!(data, pretty: true) always compact-encodes then reformats via Jason.Formatter.pretty_print_to_iodata regardless of key order, so an ordered round-trip only fixes effect (1) and still fails the minimal-diff goal) plus the decode-shape-fork argument, both of which remain valid without the false version claim. Also correct the handoff-worthy summary language ('Checked mix.exs/mix.lock directly... Jason.OrderedObject is not present in 1.4.5') for the same reason when resubmitting.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- 1 BLOCKER above (factually incorrect Jason.OrderedObject version claim in section 1.1), rework iteration 1. Recommendation of option (b) and the algorithm in section 2 need no changes; only section 1.1's stated reasoning for rejecting option (a) needs correcting to rest on the effect-(2)/decode-shape-fork grounds alone, which are independently sound.
